This is only the base model, no upgrades yet for the Pro/Max version. The memory bandwidth is 153GB/s which is not enough to run viable open source LLM models properly.

153 GB/s is not bad at all for a base model; the Nvidia DGX Spark has only 273 GB/s memory bandwidth despite being billed as a desktop 'AI supercomputer'. Models like Qwen 3 30B-A3B should run at 30+ tok/s at 4-bit quant.

It can run larger models quite slowly but lacks matmul acceleration (included in the M5) useful for context/prompt performance at inference. I will probably burn my budget on an M5 Max with 256gb, the price will be upsetting but that's life!
The memory capacity to me is an even bigger problem, at 32GB max.
Constantly at 90%+ RAM utilization with my 64GiB (VMs, IDEs etc.). Hoping to go with at least 128GiB (or more) once M5 Max is released.
I appreciate Apple propping up the GPU performance of their SoC but it feels a bit pointless when all the libraries they provide are so insular and disconnected from the rest of the industry.
The M5 MacBook Pro still gets the Broadcom WiFi chip but the M5 iPad Pros get the N1 and C1X (Sweet). All in all, apple is doing some incredible things with hardware.

32GB RAM limit on current M5 models. Now wait for M5 Max.
Did anyone else notice that the base storage has been upgraded to 512G? I knew this was coming after iPhone 17s storage upgrade!
Despite the flak Apple gets, there M-series continues to impress me as I learn more about hardware.
